subject: Deal-driven capacity bridge & activation timeline
messages:
From: Mary Chen <mary.chen@events.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@events.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted->Dedicated timing & initial sizing numbers

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. EventsAI has finalized the committed usage profile for Q1 and we need to lock a migration window to Dedicated capacity tied to the EVT-2026-430 contract. A few high-level items we need validated from Redwood:

- Expected sustained qps/throughput for our peak campaign window (we expect ~18k requests/minute; median seq len ~280 tokens).
- Suggested GPU types/config (we prefer a single variant for predictability).
- A short validation run (48h load test) and acceptance criteria before cutover.
- A proposed activation date range in early Jan (our go-live target: Jan 18-22).

I've attached the preliminary traffic spreadsheet and a CSV export of our sample workloads. Can your team confirm that the committed GPU pool (NVIDIA A40 x12 or equivalent) can sustain the SLA targets with the batching profile we discussed? If you prefer, we can push the validation later into Jan but we'd like a clear pre-cutover checklist.

Thanks,
Mary Chen
VP, Platform
EventsAI

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Mary Chen <mary.chen@events.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted->Dedicated timing & initial sizing numbers

Mary — thanks for the spreadsheet and the clear targets. We can support the Jan 18-22 window but recommend the following sequence so we have a low-risk activation and measurable acceptance gates: 

1) Sizing attestation (this week): Redwood infra + EventsAI sample workload-> run our throughput estimator and confirm GPU pool sizing.
2) Staging validation (Dec 20–22): 48h smoke + 48h sustained at 60/80/100% of expected peak. Acceptance metrics: 95th perc latency under 220ms, no more than 1% rejected tokens, and p95 CPU/GPU utilization headroom >= 12%.
3) Pre-cutover dry-run (Jan 10–11): execute canary traffic shift to Dedicated for <2 hours during a low-impact window; rollback plan validated.
4) Activation window (Jan 18–22): full traffic swap with monitoring and automatic fallback to Hosted with 30-minute SL rollback.

Preliminary recommendation: start with 12x A40s configured as 6 inference nodes with 2 cards each (shard-aware routing) + a hot KV cache layer. This gives predictable latency and allows us to scale to 24x if needed during the acceptance stage. Dev — can you prepare the staging config and an estimated cost delta if EventsAI asks for burst-to-24x?

I've attached a concise checklist (PDF) you can use with EventsAI during the attestation. I'll schedule a 30-minute sync for Friday to walk through the validation run plan.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_capacity_bridge_checklist.pdf (pdf, 28 KB)]

Quick notes after looking at the sample profile and Sofia's plan: 

- The 12x A40 approach is a reasonable starting point if EventsAI accepts a 2:1 consolidation (batching) profile. We'll need to validate the KV/cache hit rate — if it's < 65% we should recommend 16x instead.
- For the staging validation, propose the following telemetry gates: p95 latency, token generation variance, tail CPU memory OOM counts, and network egress per minute. We'll put together a smoke harness that emits synthetic traffic with the same seq-length distribution.
- Dev: schedule the canary window as an opt-in on Jan 10 during 02:00–04:00 UTC; that gives us a 30-minute steady-state check then a planned rollback. Add a quick script to flip fallback routing and assert traffic percentages.

Also — question for sales/legal: does the EVT-2026-430 contract require an SLA bonus/penalty explicitly tied to p95 latency? If so we need the legal checkbox before activation.

— Karthik

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Mary Chen <mary.chen@events.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted->Dedicated timing & initial sizing numbers

Thanks all — quick status update and next steps in prep for Jan: 

- Sizing attestation: completed (attached spreadsheet shows our estimator output). Recommendation: 14x A40 baseline to safely hit p95 goals given the sample KV hit variance; 12x is acceptable if EventsAI confirms >70% cache hit on the final workload.
- Staging validation: booked Dec 20 22:00–Dec 22 22:00 PST for the smoke + sustained runs. We will run three ramps at 60/80/100% of expected peak.
- Pre-cutover dry-run: scheduled Jan 10 02:00–04:00 UTC as Karthik suggested; will limit to 10% traffic for 30m then step to 50% for 30m. Automatic rollback will be tested.
- Activation window: Jan 18–22 is confirmed as the target; target cutover day = Jan 19 (Tues). We will provide a 24h on-call support rotation and a fallback playbook.

Open items for EventsAI: please confirm final KV/cache hit rate and whether the contract has an explicit p95 SLA clause (Marissa / sales/legal to advise). Also confirm whether you want Redwood to provision burst capacity (24x) for the first 72h post-cutover.

Mary — if this plan looks good I'll send an invite for the Friday engineering sync and share the staging runbook link.

Sofia
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
